chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no harm in the leftover water of the cat: wudu (ablution) may be performed from it and it may be drunk from. And one must not drink from the leftover water of the dog, unless it is a large basin from which water is drawn.

key_terms.حَوْضًا: a basin or reservoir of water
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or drink remaining after drinking
key_terms.فَضْلِ: leftover remainder of a drink or water after an animal has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: Can water left over by a cat or dog be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the purity and use of water after animals have drunk from it. It states that the cat’s leftover water may be used for wudu (ablution) and drinking, while the dog’s leftover water is not to be drunk except in the case of a large reservoir whose volume mitigates contamination.
